issues.legal_issue: A statutory method for assessing newly assessable private lands does not violate equal protection when it uses fair and relevant assessment factors and the challenger does not establish irrational classification or unjustified disparity.
material_facts: The statute made previously rent-exempt private lands assessable for the first time.

It classified the lands by type and set maximum rates, while requiring the assessment officer to consider soil and productivity, land class, market value, prevailing rents for similar nearby lands, and other prescribed matters.

The petitioners relied on assessments that were generally higher than rates under the existing settlement but supplied insufficient material to establish that the classification was irrational or that the assessment method materially departed from relevant settlement principles.
The new assessment regime applied pending the later settlement operations that were to cover assessable lands generally.
issues.conclusion: The petitioners failed to establish that the assessment provisions violated Article 14; the provisions laid down fair and equitable tests for determining rent.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 permits classification where it is rational and has a reasonable nexus with the statute’s object. The statute is initially presumed constitutional, and where the challenger’s material is unsatisfactory the State may rely on that presumption. The factors specified in Sections 5 and 6 were fair and substantially similar to considerations used in survey settlement; the newly assessed lands were not necessarily comparable in every respect to lands covered by the previous settlement.

rule.if: equal_protection_challenge and newly_assessed_class and assessment_uses_relevant_factors and not evidence_establishes_unjustified_disparity

predicates.equal_protection_challenge: The proceeding challenges a law or assessment method on the ground that it treats a class of landowners unequally.
predicates.newly_assessed_class: The law subjects a class of previously exempt lands to assessment for the first time.
predicates.assessment_uses_relevant_factors: The assessment method directs decision-makers to consider factors relevant to the land and to comparable assessments.
predicates.evidence_establishes_unjustified_dispari: The challenger produces sufficient evidence that the classification is irrational or that the disparity in treatment lacks a reasonable justification.

issues.definition: When an equal-protection challenge concerns a newly assessed class, relevant assessment factors and the absence of sufficient evidence of unjustified disparity lead to the assessment method not being shown to violate equal protection.

issues.legal_issue: A legislature may use a statutory definition of a constitutional term more broadly when the definition identifies the property subject to a law rather than interpreting the Constitution.
material_facts: The statute defined the relevant term to include a ruler’s relatives and dependants, making its definition broader than the definition in Article 366(22).
The statute used that definition to identify private lands subject to rent assessment, rather than to define who qualified as a ruler for purposes of the Constitution.
The legislature was competent to enact the law concerning the lands in question.
issues.conclusion: The broader statutory definition was not inconsistent with Article 366(22) and did not make the statute invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Definitions in Article 366 are intended to interpret the Constitution’s provisions, unless context otherwise requires; they do not prevent a legislature from using a broader definition in a statute to identify its subject matter. The Court also relied on the legislature’s competence over the relevant subject under Entry 18 of List II of the Seventh Schedule.

predicates.constitutional_definition_challenge: The proceeding claims that a statutory definition conflicts with a definition used in the Constitution.
predicates.statutory_term_identifies_property_subje: The statute uses the term to identify property governed by its operative provisions.
predicates.statutory_term_interprets_constitutional: The statute uses the term to determine constitutional status under the Constitution.

issues.definition: When a challenged statutory term identifies property subject to a law rather than interpreting constitutional status, a broader definition is not invalid merely because it differs from the constitutional definition.

issues.legal_issue: A law authorising an assessment or tax does not constitute deprivation, acquisition, or requisition of property merely because it imposes a payment obligation.
material_facts: The law imposed rent assessment on agricultural lands that had previously been exempt from assessment.
It authorised a levy and did not purport to take, acquire, or requisition the lands.
The challenge was to the validity of the levy under the constitutional protection concerning property.
issues.conclusion: The law was outside the purview of Article 31 because it authorised a tax levy without depriving the owners of property or acquiring or requisitioning it.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31(1) concerns deprivation of property otherwise than by authority of law, and Article 31(2) concerns compulsory acquisition or requisition; neither applies merely because a law imposes a tax. Article 31(5)(b)(i) provides that Article 31(2) does not affect laws imposing or levying a tax or penalty. The Court agreed with the decision upholding the Act in Pratap Kesari Deo v. State of Orissa, A.I.R. 1961 Orissa 131.

rule.if: property_rights_challenge and levy_only_imposes_assessment and not property_taken_or_acquired

predicates.property_rights_challenge: The proceeding challenges a law on the ground that it infringes constitutional protection of property.
predicates.levy_only_imposes_assessment: The law imposes an assessment or tax payment obligation on property.
predicates.property_taken_or_acquired: The law deprives the owner of the property or provides for its compulsory acquisition or requisition.

issues.definition: In a property-rights challenge, a law that only imposes an assessment and does not take or acquire the property is not treated as property deprivation or acquisition.
